name: Say That Again I Dare You
look: A still from Pulp Fiction. Samuel L. Jackson as Jules Winnfield, with curly hair and sideburns, in a black suit, white shirt and thin black tie, aims a silver pistol at someone off-screen with a cold, intense glare.
use: A threatening dare not to repeat something annoying. The caption follows Jules's line, 'Say [word] again, I dare you,' aimed at an overused phrase, mispronunciation or bad opinion.
examples: Say 'it's just a quick question' one more time
describe: samuel l jackson pointing a gun in pulp fiction
man in a black suit aiming a pistol and daring you
jules threatening someone with a handgun
guy with curly hair and sideburns holding a gun
angry hitman in a suit pointing a gun at someone off screen
origin: From Pulp Fiction (1994), where Jules Winnfield dares a terrified man to say 'what' one more time.
